html:
A Roman civil war fought in Spain from 80 to 72 BCE between Quintus Sertorius, a follower of Marius, and the government set up by Sulla.

Sertorius had been governor in Spain when Sulla won the civil war in Italy, and he was driven out. In 80 BCE the Lusitanians invited him back to lead them. He won over the Celtiberians too and combined native fighters with Roman exiles. He fought a war of ambushes and raids and beat several Roman commanders, including Metellus Pius.

He ran his territory like a Roman state in exile, with his own senate of exiles. At Osca he opened a school where the sons of Spanish nobles learned Latin and Greek, which also kept them as hostages. Stories say a white fawn followed him and brought him messages from the gods. Late in the war he made a deal with Mithridates VI.

From 76 BCE Rome sent the young Pompey, who struggled against him for years. The war ended only when Sertorius was murdered at a banquet in 73 or 72 BCE by his officer Perperna, whom Pompey then easily beat.
sum: A Roman civil war fought in Spain from 80 to 72 BCE between Quintus Sertorius, a follower of Marius, and the government set up by Sulla.
